The whole non-clinical side of the job

Audit, teaching, research, management, your portfolio, the system itself. You are expected to handle all of it from early in your career — and none of it was part of your clinical training.

MedLex Foundations teaches the skills that sit outside clinical knowledge but decide how capable and credible you appear: how your service is actually run, how to communicate so that colleagues listen, how to teach, audit and research with confidence, how to build a portfolio that supports your career, and how to lead a team when the time comes.

Every programme is built by a consultant who has worked inside demanding health systems in the United Kingdom, Egypt and Qatar — and knows exactly where doctors are left to work it out alone.

“If you’ve ever sat in a meeting hoping not to be asked a question, this is for you. You’re not behind — you were just never shown. We’ll show you.”MEDLEX FOUNDATIONS

Who this pathway is for

Doctors in the UK, the Gulf and other advanced systemsWorking in, or training within, a system whose unwritten rules were never explained.
Early- and mid-career doctorsConfident with patients, less sure in audit, teaching or management — and starting to think about appraisal.
Senior clinicians in management rolesLeading a service or a team, and wanting a clear method rather than instinct.
Anyone who would rather arrive preparedThe doctor who wants solid footing before walking into the room.

For clinicians. Not for the general public.

The Clinician's Edge · coming soon

8 modules. 8 skills you will use.

One online course covering the whole non-clinical side of the job. Each module explains what you will be expected to do — and what you will be able to do by the end.

01

Understanding How the System Works

Roles, hierarchy, rotas, on-call, escalation, and where you sit within it — the UK system as the worked example, with the principles that carry to the Gulf.

Walk into any department and understand how it runs.
02

Communication at Work

The referral, the email to a consultant, the notes, the handover, the moment you speak up in a meeting — clear, concise, and escalated the right way.

Communicate with the clarity colleagues expect of you.
03

Audit & Quality Improvement

What audit and QI actually are, how the cycle works from standard to re-audit, the difference between the two, and what you will be asked to do.

Take part in audit and QI with real understanding.
04

Research

The main types of study and what they are for, what being involved means early on, how to get onto a project, and how to read a paper well enough to discuss it.

Hold a conversation about a paper and find a route onto a project.
05

Teaching, Supervision & Feedback

Planning and delivering a clear teaching session, supervising juniors, giving feedback that helps — and receiving it well.

Teach and supervise in a way that strengthens how you are seen.
06

Management & Leadership Basics

How a service is organised, who the key people are, how to work within a team, and the real difference between management and leadership at your level.

Step into team and leadership situations with confidence.
07

Portfolio, Appraisal & Revalidation

What a portfolio is, what to collect and why, how appraisal works, and how revalidation fits into the longer arc of a career.

Know exactly what to collect, from the first day.
08

Preparing for an Internal Investigation

The subject no one prepares you for. What an investigation involves, your rights, what to do and avoid early on, and where to find proper support.

Understand how investigations work and protect yourself sensibly.

Questions.

Who is this pathway for?

Doctors working in or training within the UK, the Gulf or another advanced health system; early- and mid-career doctors who were never taught the non-clinical side of the job; and senior clinicians in management roles who want a clear method. It is not for the general public.

What is available now?

The Clinician's Edge opens first, at founding-cohort pricing announced to the waitlist. The Clinical Leadership Programme and AI for Clinicians follow — dates go to the waitlist first.

How is The Clinician's Edge delivered?

Fully online and self-paced: short video lessons, interactive pages in each module, and a workbook and toolkit you keep.

How is the Clinical Leadership Programme delivered?

Live and face to face, in small cohorts hosted by city. The language — Arabic or English — follows the location.

Is it in English or Arabic?

The Clinician's Edge is in English. The Clinical Leadership Programme runs in Arabic or English depending on where the cohort is held. Each programme states its language on its own page.

Is the pathway accredited or CPD-certified?

Programmes are independent and not currently accredited by any college or regulator. You receive a certificate of completion. CPD recognition will be shown on each programme page once it is in place.

Is this clinical training?

No. Foundations covers the professional, non-clinical skills of a medical career. It does not teach clinical medicine and does not replace specialty training or local induction.

MedLex is a specialist professional education and training company at the intersection of medicine, law and institutional practice — founded and led by a UK-trained Consultant Forensic Psychiatrist.
